package singleton_test

import (
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/utils/singleton"
	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

func TestSingleton(t *testing.T) {
	RegisterFailHandler(Fail)
	RunSpecs(t, "Singleton Suite")
}

var _ = Describe("Get", func() {
	type T struct{ id string }
	var numInstances int
	constructor := func() interface{} {
		numInstances++
		return &T{id: uuid.NewString()}
	}

	It("calls the constructor to create a new instance", func() {
		instance := singleton.Get(T{}, constructor)
		Expect(numInstances).To(Equal(1))
		Expect(instance).To(BeAssignableToTypeOf(&T{}))
	})

	It("does not call the constructor the next time", func() {
		instance := singleton.Get(T{}, constructor)
		newInstance := singleton.Get(T{}, constructor)

		Expect(newInstance.(*T).id).To(Equal(instance.(*T).id))
		Expect(numInstances).To(Equal(1))
	})

	It("does not call the constructor even if a pointer is passed as the object", func() {
		instance := singleton.Get(T{}, constructor)
		newInstance := singleton.Get(&T{}, constructor)

		Expect(newInstance.(*T).id).To(Equal(instance.(*T).id))
		Expect(numInstances).To(Equal(1))
	})

	It("only calls the constructor once when called concurrently", func() {
		const maxCalls = 2000
		var numCalls int32
		start := sync.WaitGroup{}
		start.Add(1)
		prepare := sync.WaitGroup{}
		prepare.Add(maxCalls)
		done := sync.WaitGroup{}
		done.Add(maxCalls)
		for i := 0; i < maxCalls; i++ {
			go func() {
				start.Wait()
				singleton.Get(T{}, constructor)
				atomic.AddInt32(&numCalls, 1)
				done.Done()
			}()
			prepare.Done()
		}
		prepare.Wait()
		start.Done()
		done.Wait()

		Expect(numCalls).To(Equal(int32(maxCalls)))
		Expect(numInstances).To(Equal(1))
	})
})

item.text: The package currently serializes the legacy `Get` calls through a background goroutine and keys them by a pointer-stripped type name. I’ll leave that API intact and add a separate generic cache keyed by the exact Go type, so `T` and `*T` remain independent while calls for each type share a `sync.Once` entry.

`GetInstance` now uses the exact generic type as its cache key, and a per-type `sync.Once` protects construction. The package tests pass, including a new check that launches 20,000 concurrent calls and confirms they all receive the same pointer from one constructor execution. I’m checking the legacy callers and race behavior next.

The 20,000-call test also passes under Go’s race detector. The packages that use the legacy `Get` API (`server/events`, `core/scrobbler`, and `scheduler`) pass; the `db` package test is still running.

Implemented `singleton.GetInstance[T]` in `utils/singleton/singleton.go`. The cache uses exact `reflect.Type` keys and per-type `sync.Once` initialization, keeping `T` and `*T` independent. A typed wrapper preserves nil interface results.

Added package coverage for value and pointer separation, reuse, nil interface results, and 20,000 concurrent calls.

Validation passed:
- `go test ./utils/singleton`
- `go test -race ./utils/singleton`
- `go test ./server/events ./core/scrobbler ./scheduler ./db`

The sqlite3 C compiler emitted an existing warning about `sqlite3SelectNew` potentially returning a local address; the `db` tests passed.

item.text:
Implemented generic `GetInstance[T]` in [singleton.go](/app/utils/singleton/singleton.go). It caches by exact type, runs each type’s constructor once under concurrency, and keeps value and pointer singletons independent.

Added tests in [singleton_test.go](/app/utils/singleton/singleton_test.go), including 20,000 concurrent calls and nil interface results.

Validation passed: `go test ./utils/singleton`, `go test -race ./utils/singleton`, and the packages using legacy `Get`. The `db` tests passed with a compiler warning from sqlite3.
